thread:
dave: Quick follow-up from the PM postmortem on the kv-cache OOM series. Action items + owners below. Root cause summary: small, persistent allocations during compaction + arena fragmentation + delayed slab purge. We need immediate mitigations and medium-term instrumentation.

priya: Thanks. I captured a minimal repro on dev: repeated kv_put/kv_delete under compaction pressure. Command I used to stress: 
```bash
# spawn workload that toggles compaction
wrk -t4 -c100 -d120s --script=kv_compact_workload.lua http://localhost:8080
# capture jemalloc stats periodically
while true; do echo "--- $(date)"; cat /proc/$(pidof runtime)/status | egrep "VmRSS|VmPeak"; sleep 5; done
```
The RSS climbs steadily and doesn't return after compaction. Heap profiles: uploaded to INF-KV-3081.

ben: Short mitigations I'm proposing and will own: 1) enable jemalloc background purge by default in staging, 2) add a post-compact free sweep to release tombstones, 3) temp soft cap on in-memory index at 65% for 48h. ETA: 36h for flags + tests.

elaine: I'll add observability: new metrics runtime.kv.compact_count, runtime.kv.live_refs, runtime.kv.fragmentation_ratio. Will also create Grafana alert that fires at fragmentation_ratio > 0.6 and RSS > 80% for 5m. ETA: EOD tomorrow.

ops-bot: Created ticket INF-KV-3081: "kv-cache-oom-followup" assigned to ben, elaine, priya. Priority: P1. Link: https://redwood.internal/inf/INF-KV-3081

ci-bot: Automated canary rollback triggered on service/kv-core (reason: elevated RSS on v1.4.2 canary). Rollback to v1.4.1 completed at 1800126845.

dave: To be explicit on owners/dates: 
- Ben: implement post-compact sweep + jemalloc purge flag + unit tests (short) — ETA 36h
- Elaine: dashboards + alerting + add per-shard live_refs metric (short) — ETA 48h
- Priya: collect 5 heap profiles under different loads and attach kernel/version metadata (short) — ETA 72h
- Dave: coordinate Dedicated-customer opt-in config and legal/account notes (short) — ETA EOD Fri
- All: 1-week follow-up sync to review telemetry and decide on refactor of compaction path (recurring) — schedule next Wednesday

priya: One more data point: older nodes (linux 4.14) show worse fragmentation in profiles. I've marked kernel in the profile uploads.

ben: I'll open a PR with a toggle: runtime.config.kv.post_compact_reclaim = true|false. We'll default to off for Dedicated until we get legal sign-off. PR: https://git.redwood/eng-runtime/pulls/930

elaine: Added Grafana panels in the runtime dashboard and a dashboard row for the canary. Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/d/runtime/kv-oom (please review).

dave: For Dedicated customers: let's expose a support KB describing the tradeoffs (possible short GC pauses vs lower long-term RSS). I'll draft and loop in account.

priya: Staging canary window booked tomorrow 09:30 PT. I'll run the workload script and post the time-series.

ops-bot: INF-KV-3081 updated: labels: postmortem-followup, priority/P1, owner-set.

ben: Note for the runbook: alarm should attempt soft scale-down of cache first (reduce in-memory cap), then trigger operator page if soft-scale doesn't reduce RSS in 10 minutes. I'll add this to the runbook PR.

ci-bot: CI check flagged one flaky allocator test; Ben will address in the PR.

dave: Great. Keep updates in INF-KV-3081. We'll do a short summary to #all-hands after the 1-week sync. If anyone hits blockers, DM me. :eyes:
